notes: rust-stdlib-crypto: the Hash identifiers with New, Available, Size, HashFunc, String and RegisterHash. MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2 and SHA-3 are registered; MD4, RIPEMD-160, BLAKE2, MD5SHA1 and MLDSAMu exist as variants but are unavailable, as in a Go program that does not import their packages. The key, signing, decryption and KEM interfaces are traits: PublicKey, PrivateKey and DecrypterOpts are aliases of dyn Any (Go's empty interface); Go's nil rand reader is None; Go's signer.(MessageSigner) type assertion, which a trait object cannot express, is the provided method Signer::as_message_signer that SignMessage consults. The key types implement them: ed25519, ecdsa, rsa and mldsa private keys are Signers (rsa also a Decrypter, with Hash and the packages' option types as SignerOpts through SignerOpts::as_any), and the mlkem keys are Encapsulators and Decapsulators.

Decrypter.Decrypt.note: rand and opts are optional (Go passes nil); decrypt is Decrypt(nil, ...); decrypt_with_rng takes the reader

DecrypterOpts.note: alias of dyn Any: Go's empty interface

Hash.New.note: Returns an error where Go panics when the hash is unavailable.

Hash.Size.note: the enum cannot hold the out-of-range values for which Go panics

MessageSigner.SignMessage.note: sign_message is SignMessage(nil, ...); sign_message_with_rng takes the reader

PrivateKey.note: alias of dyn Any: Go's empty interface

PublicKey.note: alias of dyn Any: Go's empty interface

SignMessage.note: Go's interface upgrade signer.(MessageSigner) is Signer::as_message_signer; Go's reader argument becomes `sign_message_with_rng`, which takes the reader after the signer; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005).

Signer.Sign.note: rand is optional (Go passes nil); opts is a &dyn SignerOpts; sign is Sign(nil, ...); sign_with_rng is Sign(rng, ...) (ADR 0005)

SignerOpts.HashFunc.note: None is Go's zero Hash (the message was not hashed)
